references.text: The verse in John points to the fact that Jesus was to die a specific death (crucifixion), which corresponds with the prophecy in Isaiah that he would be counted among transgressors and pour out his life unto death.

In this early chapter of the Gospel of John, Jesus explains that he must be "lifted up" in the same way Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, which is a direct reference to the manner of death (crucifixion) mentioned in 12:33.
Jesus explicitly predicts here that when he is "lifted up," people will recognize who he truly is, directly linking to the explanation in 12:33 that he would die a specific death.
Here Jesus confirms that the prophecy in 12:33 concerning his death is about to be fulfilled by specifying that he will die in a way distinct from others (crucifixion).
